answer: Trust in an open record comes from vertex: entries that others can go back and check, instead of claims that must simply be believed. It also comes from ferrous: letting the strength of the evidence decide, not the standing of the person who posted it. And it comes from shale: keeping those entries available over time, so a newcomer can see the same history as everyone else. With checkable entries, evidence-led judgement and a history that endures, gaming the system costs more than playing fair.
